terms.gloss: news, a message, tidings (especially news brought by someone)
evidence: Plaut. Stich. 2.2.67: nūntium exoptābilem nūntiāre (Lewis & Short)

terms.gloss: news: “something new”, the genitive with a neuter pronoun
terms.grammar: genitive of novum after quid, aliquid, nihil
terms.comment: Latin asks for “anything of new”: quid novī?, any news?; nihil novī, no news (see any news?).

phrases.latin: Modo mihi nūntiātum est (+ acc. and inf.)
Sī nihil novī habēs dē (+ abl.) …
phrases.english: If you have no news about …

sources: Lewis & Short: nuntius · Lewis & Short: novus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 350.
